claims: Artemis 2 reached a peak speed of approximately 25,000 mph (~40,000 km/h) during its re-entry into Earth's atmosphere on April 10, 2026.
Approximately 25,000 mph is necessary for the Orion capsule to return from the Moon.
Artemis 2's peak re-entry speed is more than 30 times the speed of sound.
Artemis 2's peak re-entry speed matches the fastest speeds experienced by humans.
The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket reached over 17,000 mph during the launch of Artemis 2 to reach orbit.
The spacecraft traveled at approximately 24,527 mph (39,472 km/h) during the translunar injection (TLI) of Artemis 2 to leave Earth's orbit for the Moon.
Orion entered the atmosphere at roughly 24,000 to 25,000 mph during the re-entry of Artemis 2.
The capsule slowed to roughly 17 mph during the splashdown of Artemis 2 using a series of parachutes.
During the high-speed re-entry of Artemis 2, the capsule's heat shield protected the crew from temperatures exceeding 10,000°C (over 18,000°F).
